bull_bear.body:
- Jayhawk acquisition (~$150Mn total consideration) funded through a combination of internal accruals, debt and quasi equity.
- Bliss GVS Pharma acquisition structured via a non-controlling non-voting equity instrument (~₹1,300 Cr) plus a term loan (~₹300 Cr), avoiding a straightforward equity stake purchase.
- Growth phase (2023-24) financed through capital markets: ₹5,000 Mn QIP and ₹5,500 Mn Preferential Issue.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Custom synthesis / CSM model with multistep synthesis and complex chemical reaction capability, giving high technical barriers to entry — 'technical complexity, long qualification cycles and deep customer collaboration create durable competitive advantage'
- Long-term contracts and LOIs with domestic and global customers spanning periods of up to 10 years
- Over 200+ domestic and international customers, with 90+ molecules under development and 65+ pharma and polymer molecules at R&D and pilot stage
- Two DSIR-recognised R&D centres and a team of over 90 scientists driving in-house process innovation and cost optimisation
- Backward integration into fluorine chemistry through Tanfac (access to HF and KF), giving control over critical inputs
- Multi-geography manufacturing after the Jayhawk acquisition, adding US customer proximity and access to regulated markets
- Renewable energy accounts for nearly 60.35% of electricity consumed across manufacturing operations, supported by a 27.5 MW solar and hybrid renewable plant
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Agrochemical cyclicality and customer destocking — Management names agrochemical cyclicality among the Company's threats, and the AR describes the segment as having faced a subdued demand environment in prior periods that only revived in FY 2025-26 as channel inventory levels normalised. Agrochemicals remain the single largest standalone revenue contributor, so the cycle drives group volumes.
- Raw material price volatility and import dependency — Management flags raw material price and supply volatility as a threat. The MD&A adds that the Indian chemicals sector remains reliant on imported raw materials despite strong export growth, exposing it to global supply-chain disruption and price volatility, and that an inverted duty structure — higher duties on raw materials than on finished products — raises production costs and makes imports more competitive.
- Export and foreign-exchange exposure with geographic concentration shifts — Exports were 50.17% of turnover (BRSR Section A item 19) across 14 countries, and management lists foreign exchange fluctuation among its threats. The geographic mix moved sharply within one year — North America from 3% to 26% of standalone revenue while India + SEZ fell from 62% to 50% and Europe from 11% to 4% — so revenue is sensitive to conditions in a small number of destination markets.
- Geopolitical, tariff and trade-policy disruption — The MD&A names global trade and geopolitical risks explicitly: geopolitical tensions, potential tariffs and anti-dumping actions create uncertainty for export markets and can disrupt supply chains, complicating sourcing strategies and increasing costs for companies reliant on cross-border trade — directly relevant given half of turnover is exported and a newly acquired US manufacturing base.
- Regulatory and decarbonisation compliance cost — Management lists evolving regulatory requirements as a threat, and the MD&A states that adopting low-carbon technologies and meeting stringent environmental regulations requires significant capital investment, with the transition to low-carbon processes and feedstocks being capital-intensive and complex amid high energy costs. A hazardous-chemistry manufacturer carries EPR obligations and pollution-control capex on top of this.
- Acquisition integration and leverage risk — The Jayhawk/Monitchem Target Group acquisition completed on February 27, 2026 was funded through a combination of external borrowings and other financing arrangements availed by the Company and its group entities, along with guarantees, security interests and credit support provided by the Company. FY 2025-26 carried only one month of Jayhawk's contribution, so the synergy case is unproven, and a further controlling-stake acquisition of Bliss GVS Pharma is pending.
- Customer and channel concentration — The business is a B2B custom-synthesis model serving agrochemical and pharmaceutical MNCs, where sales to the top 10 dealers/distributors were 99.4% of sales to dealers/distributors and purchases from the top 10 trading houses were 96.67% of purchases from trading houses (BRSR open-ness of business, standalone). Long-term contracts and LOIs of up to 10 years are a strength but also concentrate revenue in few counterparties.
- Competitive overcapacity and margin pressure in global chemicals — The MD&A records that total shareholder returns in the chemicals industry have lagged and flattened owing to rising capital costs, shrinking margins from higher input costs and weaker end-market demand, and that regional overcapacity plus new plant start-ups is pressuring global prices and margins. Management separately names competition from established global and regional players as a threat.

business.body: Incorporated in 2003 and tracing its operations to 1984, the Company undertakes multistep synthesis and complex chemical reactions to make customised speciality chemicals used as intermediates in its customers' manufacturing processes. It operates two verticals — Life science-related Speciality Chemicals (agrochemicals, personal care and pharmaceuticals) and Performance Materials (electronics & EV chemicals and polymers) — on a business-to-business model serving agrochemical and pharmaceutical MNCs in India and abroad. Exports contributed 50.17% of turnover and the Company is recognised by the Government of India as a three-star export house.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Diversify the portfolio beyond agrochemicals into pharmaceuticals, personal care, polymers and electronic chemicals to expand the addressable market and reduce dependence on any single segment
- Shift deliberately towards higher-value, technology-intensive applications where technical complexity and long qualification cycles create entry barriers
- Grow through strategic acquisitions into adjacent markets — Jayhawk Fine Chemicals (US, completed February 2026) and a controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma (definitive agreement signed)
- Build a globally integrated speciality chemicals and CDMO platform spanning India and the United States, with upstream fluorination inputs from Tanfac and downstream high-purity capability from Jayhawk
- Move the operating focus from capacity creation to capacity utilisation, commercial execution and customer acquisition now that the multi-year capex programme is complete
- Sustain innovation through DSIR-recognised R&D, a team of over 90 scientists and a pipeline of more than 90 molecules at various stages of evaluation and commercialisation
- Develop in-house innovative processes for complex chemistries and pursue cost optimisation
- Reduce environmental intensity through renewable power (solar and hybrid wind-solar) and resource efficiency, targeting Energy Net Zero by 2027
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company completed the final phase of its multi-year capital expenditure programme during FY 2025-26, with all major facilities now commissioned and commercialised; having doubled manufacturing capacity over the last three years, its focus is shifting from capacity creation towards capacity utilisation, commercial execution and customer acquisition, which management expects to support operating leverage and cash generation without a significant incremental capital requirement in the near term. Expansion during the year came through acquisition rather than greenfield build: pursuant to a Sale and Purchase Agreement with CABB Europe GmbH approved by the Board on December 09, 2025, the rights were assigned to wholly owned subsidiary Doriath S.a r.l., Luxembourg, which completed the acquisition of the Target Group (Monitchem Kansas S.a r.l. with Kansas HoldCo Inc., Kansas HoldCo 1, Inc. and Jayhawk Fine Chemicals Corporation) on February 27, 2026, funded through a combination of external borrowings and other financing arrangements with guarantees and credit support from the Company; Monitchem Kansas S.a r.l. was subsequently liquidated on June 30, 2026. Jayhawk brings a production facility in Kansas, United States of roughly 3 million sq. m with an ~800 acre land bank that is less than 10% utilised, and began contributing to revenue from 27 February 2026. The Company has also signed a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma, which together with Jayhawk is expected to broaden participation across the speciality chemicals and pharmaceutical value chains in the years ahead. Renewable capacity supporting the plants comprises a 27.5 MW solar and hybrid renewable energy plant. NOTE — THE REPORT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON FOOTPRINT AND CAPACITY: the Directors' Report states 'six manufacturing facilities in Gujarat, India, with four facilities located at Sachin, Surat, and two located at Jhagadia, Bharuch, with an aggregate installed capacity of about 30,000 MT, as of March 31, 2026', while the MD&A Company Overview states the Company 'operates eight manufacturing facilities across India and the United States, with a combined installed capacity exceeding 200,000 MT' and BRSR Section A item 18 reports 7 national plants plus 1 international. Neither capacity figure is labelled standalone or consolidated, and the two differ by nearly 7x, so the consolidated capacity is treated as disputed and is not recorded below.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Increasing outsourcing of speciality chemistries by global innovators and growing demand for specialised chemistries creates opportunity for manufacturers with technical capability and reliable platforms
- Global supply-chain diversification and the China-plus-one sourcing strategy continue to channel investment and customer interest towards Indian manufacturers with scale, technology and compliance credentials
- Agrochemical demand recovered as channel inventory normalised and customer offtake improved; the segment saw a healthy revival during the year
- Pharmaceutical and polymer businesses continued to build momentum, supported by the ramp-up of recently commercialised molecules
- Strengthening demand from customers in the United States and Japan, with Japan emerging as a meaningful contributor to revenue; deepening engagement in Europe
- Management expects the benefits of Jayhawk integration and synergy creation to become increasingly visible, FY 2025-26 having included only one month of its financial contribution
- Completed capacity additions are expected to support operating leverage and cash generation without a significant incremental capital requirement in the near term
- Favourable Indian macro backdrop — real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY 2025-26 — with monsoon-supported rural demand underpinning demand for crop protection chemistries
- Domestic speciality chemicals market estimated at approximately US$64 billion with growth expected in the high single to low double digits, supported by import substitution and rising exports
- Management remains optimistic about sustaining the growth momentum in the coming years
- Headwinds flagged: agrochemical cyclicality, raw material price and supply volatility, foreign exchange fluctuation, evolving regulatory requirements and competition from established global and regional players
- Long-term contracts and LOIs with domestic and global customers spanning a period of up to 10 years underpin the Company's growth prospects (Directors' Report, Business information)
- Development pipeline of more than 90 molecules, with 65+ pharma and polymer molecules in R&D and pilot stages; portfolio expanded to 125+ products

The Company has also signed a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma, which together with Jayhawk is expected to broaden participation across the speciality chemicals and pharmaceutical value chains in the years ahead. risks.note: Management names agrochemical cyclicality among the Company's threats, and the AR describes the segment as having faced a subdued demand environment in prior periods that only revived in FY 2025-26 as channel inventory levels normalised. Agrochemicals remain the single largest standalone revenue contributor, so the cycle drives group volumes.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and import dependency
risks.note: Management flags raw material price and supply volatility as a threat. The MD&A adds that the Indian chemicals sector remains reliant on imported raw materials despite strong export growth, exposing it to global supply-chain disruption and price volatility, and that an inverted duty structure — higher duties on raw materials than on finished products — raises production costs and makes imports more competitive.

risks.risk: Export and foreign-exchange exposure with geographic concentration shifts
risks.note: Exports were 50.17% of turnover (BRSR Section A item 19) across 14 countries, and management lists foreign exchange fluctuation among its threats. The geographic mix moved sharply within one year — North America from 3% to 26% of standalone revenue while India + SEZ fell from 62% to 50% and Europe from 11% to 4% — so revenue is sensitive to conditions in a small number of destination markets.

The MD&A names global trade and geopolitical risks explicitly: geopolitical tensions, potential tariffs and anti-dumping actions create uncertainty for export markets and can disrupt supply chains, complicating sourcing strategies and increasing costs for companies reliant on cross-border trade — directly relevant given half of turnover is exported and a newly acquired US manufacturing base.

Management lists evolving regulatory requirements as a threat, and the MD&A states that adopting low-carbon technologies and meeting stringent environmental regulations requires significant capital investment, with the transition to low-carbon processes and feedstocks being capital-intensive and complex amid high energy costs. A hazardous-chemistry manufacturer carries EPR obligations and pollution-control capex on top of this.

The Jayhawk/Monitchem Target Group acquisition completed on February 27, 2026 was funded through a combination of external borrowings and other financing arrangements availed by the Company and its group entities, along with guarantees, security interests and credit support provided by the Company. FY 2025-26 carried only one month of Jayhawk's contribution, so the synergy case is unproven, and a further controlling-stake acquisition of Bliss GVS Pharma is pending.

The business is a B2B custom-synthesis model serving agrochemical and pharmaceutical MNCs, where sales to the top 10 dealers/distributors were 99.4% of sales to dealers/distributors and purchases from the top 10 trading houses were 96.67% of purchases from trading houses (BRSR open-ness of business, standalone). Long-term contracts and LOIs of up to 10 years are a strength but also concentrate revenue in few counterparties.

risks.risk: Competitive overcapacity and margin pressure in global chemicals
risks.note: The MD&A records that total shareholder returns in the chemicals industry have lagged and flattened owing to rising capital costs, shrinking margins from higher input costs and weaker end-market demand, and that regional overcapacity plus new plant start-ups is pressuring global prices and margins. Management separately names competition from established global and regional players as a threat.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 2003 and tracing its operations to 1984, the Company undertakes multistep synthesis and complex chemical reactions to make customised speciality chemicals used as intermediates in its customers' manufacturing processes. It operates two verticals — Life science-related Speciality Chemicals (agrochemicals, personal care and pharmaceuticals) and Performance Materials (electronics & EV chemicals and polymers) — on a business-to-business model serving agrochemical and pharmaceutical MNCs in India and abroad. Exports contributed 50.17% of turnover and the Company is recognised by the Government of India as a three-star export house.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Increasing outsourcing of speciality chemistries by global innovators and growing demand for specialised chemistries creates opportunity for manufacturers with technical capability and reliable platforms
- Global supply-chain diversification and the China-plus-one sourcing strategy continue to channel investment and customer interest towards Indian manufacturers with scale, technology and compliance credentials
- Agrochemical demand recovered as channel inventory normalised and customer offtake improved; the segment saw a healthy revival during the year
- Pharmaceutical and polymer businesses continued to build momentum, supported by the ramp-up of recently commercialised molecules
- Strengthening demand from customers in the United States and Japan, with Japan emerging as a meaningful contributor to revenue; deepening engagement in Europe
- Management expects the benefits of Jayhawk integration and synergy creation to become increasingly visible, FY 2025-26 having included only one month of its financial contribution
- Completed capacity additions are expected to support operating leverage and cash generation without a significant incremental capital requirement in the near term
- Favourable Indian macro backdrop — real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY 2025-26 — with monsoon-supported rural demand underpinning demand for crop protection chemistries
- Domestic speciality chemicals market estimated at approximately US$64 billion with growth expected in the high single to low double digits, supported by import substitution and rising exports
- Management remains optimistic about sustaining the growth momentum in the coming years
- Headwinds flagged: agrochemical cyclicality, raw material price and supply volatility, foreign exchange fluctuation, evolving regulatory requirements and competition from established global and regional players
- Long-term contracts and LOIs with domestic and global customers spanning a period of up to 10 years underpin the Company's growth prospects (Directors' Report, Business information)
- Development pipeline of more than 90 molecules, with 65+ pharma and polymer molecules in R&D and pilot stages; portfolio expanded to 125+ products

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
